inputs.input: I finish it—Razor Cut through its throat while it sets itself.
I skin nothing and rest a few minutes by the stream, then move on to look for the third otterhound's tracks along the gravel bars.
I rest for half an hour by the stream, then follow the tracks upstream along the open gravel bar toward the crossing, staying alert.
I close the distance fast across the bar and, once within range, loose Fan of Blades to hit both hounds at once.
I finish the wounded one first—Razor Cut through Otterhound D's throat.
I finish the last hound—Razor Cut through Otterhound C's throat.
I head back toward the Guild hall in town to turn in the completed otterhound cull.
I ask the clerk what contracts are on the board suitable for a Novice—preferably nothing that needs a full day in the field before I've healed.
I buy the Primer of Mend for 80 copper and read it to learn the skill.
I ask the clerk how the primer is actually used—reading alone didn't teach me the skill.

I answer honestly: 'Barely a trickle, if anything. Maybe this one wasn't for me.' I ask whether the Guild buys back primers, or buys otterhound pelts and fangs, and where I can find lodging for the night.
I sell her the lot—four pelts and nine fangs—at the desk price.

sale.prose:
"Say the word" was all the word she needed. She pulled the materials ledger across, laid the pelts out fur-up, and went through the fangs one by one, tapping each onto the wood.

"Pelts, river-condition, cured but not tanned—two copper each, eight the lot. Fangs, intact, no splits—she held one up to the window light—a copper apiece, nine." She wrote the sum at the bottom of the line. "Seventeen copper for everything. That's desk price, same as I'd pay the next man."

She reached under the counter for her coin box and waited, lid half lifted, eyes on him.

"Seventeen copper, four pelts, nine fangs. Done?"

marla.prose:
The allotments lay quiet under the morning, wisps of woodsmoke from the cottages beyond the hedges. Marla was where he'd left her, bent over a bed of winter greens, tugging at the edge of a cloth cover. She straightened when his boots came up the path, the fork still in her hand.

"Well?"

He told her it was dead. She let out a long breath and looked past him toward the stream, as if expecting to see proof carried up the bank.

"In the drain itself? In its bed?" She laughed once, short and dry, and shook her head. "Sleeping in its own larder. There's a justice in that." She came along the fence line a few steps, looking down at the flattened run where it had come through. "Three weeks it's had off us. I'll tell Doss — he'd stopped coming out of an evening to check his beans. He'll sleep." She rested her weight on the fork. "You did a clean morning's work, mage. The gardens will remember it longer than you will."

He left her to her cabbages and took the path back toward Alderwatch, the morning well along now, cart ruts drying hard in the road and the weir's noise fading behind him. The town received him in its ordinary noise — a chandler's boy hauling baskets, two women arguing cheerfully about a pig, the smell of bread somewhere deep in a side lane — and the Guild hall stood open on its corner, door swinging, the smell of ink and lamp oil inside.

The broad woman with ink-stained fingers was at the counter. She looked up from her ledger as he approached.

He laid the contract slip on the wood. She picked it up, turned it toward the light, and her thumb found the seal.

"READY, and there it is." She pressed the slip against the counter, drew a line through the entry in her roll, and counted out the payout. "Forty copper for the Millbrook marten. That closes it." The coins slid across to him in a neat stack. "Anything else on your mind, or was that the morning's work?"

thread.t7.1.text: The night watch on the gap passed with nothing crossing it; the marten never showed at the fence seam.

thread.t8.1.text: Marla's neighbor Doss's chicken coop was raided by the marten on Tuesday

thread.t14.1.text: The gap behind Doss's run is a long-used marten way in, but whether the beast still uses it this morning is unknown; fresh tracking there failed

thread.t17.1.text: A dog's nails clicked once inside Doss's house, then silence — Doss keeps a dog now at the coop

thread.t24.1.text: The stone drain by the stream shows heavy marten use — beaten bank, fishbones, and now fresh clawed paw prints leading in and out at its lip; the dark interior runs back beyond the morning light.

thread.t26.1.text: The marten has come to the baited bank and is staring at Alaric's cover, deciding whether to bolt
thread.t26.1.resolution: the grey-marsh marten died in the stone drain, struck by an Arcane Bolt as it gathered to spring

thread.t35.1.text: Odo warns that a pelt buyer named Halvard tells everyone the tails are rubbed to knock the price down

thread.t36.1.text: Halvard works on at his beam, ignoring the visitor; a bell-pull by the door is there for service

thread.t38.1.text: Halvard offers to buy future grey-marsh or other worthwhile pelts first, at better-than-market prices, no haggling

thread.t39.1.text: The third serpent's fresh trail runs from the den's rear gap down the terrace slope toward the lower cut where the haul road bends through the rocks, hours old
thread.t39.1.resolution: the trail led to the seep where the young serpent lies on a ledge above the puddle

thread.t43.1.text: The wounded old ridge serpent has closed to a body-length on the flat, strike gathering; it did not fall despite the cracked scales.
thread.t43.1.resolution: the old serpent died to the Arcane Bolt before its strike landed

thread.t61.1.text: Something has raided Marla Otterwell's brassicas three nights running, leaving a low tunnel through the fence-side growth
thread.t61.1.resolution: the marten responsible for three nights of raids was killed in its drain den

thread.t68.1.text: The tallyman confirms the mule story: it was Bren's mule, a week gone, and Bren swears a big serpent came off the top shelf right onto the animal's back in the deep second cutting — might be the same

thread.t69.1.text: Fresh ridge serpent slither-marks in the deep second cutting: one under the stone shelf halfway down the slope, one in the eastern ditch climbing over the rim; the bend ahead hides the far end
thread.t69.1.resolution: the slither-mark led over the eastern rim to a lived-in serpent den under the stone slab, where the serpent itself lies coiled

thread.t71.1.text: Slither-marks along the cutting rim were wide as a forearm, and no single serpent made every one of them — more ridge serpents remain in the quarry country

thread.t72.1.text: The dry streambed gully is a shared passage: every serpent track came into or out of it, and the wind carried layered musk of more than one beast using the same route

thread.t74.1.text: The great ridge serpent at the saddle is lowering itself toward the haul road where two quarrymen work below
thread.t74.1.resolution: Alaric's Arcane Wave broke it mid-slither off the boulders; it died before it finished falling

thread.t80.1.text: Cold air and a smell of wet chalk and old earth push up the dark stair; below lie coffins, doors, and whatever broke the first adventurer's arm somewhere down in the round gallery

thread.t82.1.text: The knock heard earlier did not repeat; the passage behind the door shows no tracks and no movement, only a slid coffin lid in the dark

thread.t83.1.text: The three men's boot prints, one dragging his right leg, descend the narrow stair behind the coffin lid; no prints come back up. The lid's inner face bears the hurried warning LOW AND DARK.

thread.t89.1.text: From the gap in the slid bier lid came a slow scrape of bone on stone when the lantern light touched it
thread.t89.1.resolution: Alaric peered through the gap and saw the moving hand itself, dragging the forearm toward the lid's edge

thread.t92.1.text: A second way down from the bier chamber, used by the three men (one dragging a heel) who left the lid only loosely reseated; the cold, dry passage below runs past the lantern's throw.

thread.t94.1.text: From below the hidden stair comes a slow, rhythmic scrape, stone on stone, patient and unceasing — whoever keeps this level works down there and has heard nothing yet
thread.t94.1.resolution: the scrape was the armoured skeleton Warden scouring the wall

thread.t105.1.text: Long wake-lines lie on the shallows where fish moved — or where something else did
thread.t105.1.resolution: the search found the lurker's drag-trail and eaten pike at the churned hummocks

thread.t115.1.text: Two fresh shed ridge serpent skins, papery and big around as a man's wrist, lie snagged in the scrub at the third switchback slab.
thread.t115.1.resolution: Alaric picked up the shed skins on the terrace scrub

thread.t116.1.text: The quarryman's voice came again, closer, calling up toward the barrier: 'Oi! Did it get him? Somebody look down the third bend!' — boots clattering on broken stone below the switchback.

thread.t119.1.text: A ridge serpent lies on the overhang above the deep second cutting's top shelf, right behind Alaric, near the stain where Bren's mule died — likely the third serpent that dropped on the mule.
thread.t119.1.resolution: the serpent came over the overhang and was killed by a single Arcane Wave

thread.t127.1.text: Something else clicked and answered from beyond the bend of the upper gallery, unseen past the edge of the dark.

thread.t128.1.text: Narrow deliberate drag-marks in the floor dust run along the wall gutter for a dozen paces and turn down a side passage, out of sight

thread.t130.1.text: A circle crossed by a single bar is scratched into the fitted slab at the right passage's mouth; the left passage's floor is swept clean and something pale gleams in its far dark.

actions: 1. NOTHING TO DO — he holds F-Rank Restless Skeleton Bone already.
2. NOTHING TO DO — he holds F-Rank Restless Skeleton Grave Dust already.

3. GOES — to the corridor sloping down past the chamber's far side (the story decides whether and where he arrives). Carry the way forward in this reply until he arrives, something acts on him, or a real choice of way appears; a sound, a shadow or a track without consequence is passed in a clause, never a stop.
extra: DUNGEON AHEAD (the engine's) — the next part of level 1 he goes into holds no foe: a room, a find, a fork or a sign of what lies further; no fight there. Carry the walk to it, not further.
The way down to level 2 is sealed until level 1's guardian falls: he cannot go down yet.

inputs.input: I thank the tally-keeper, pick up the two fresh shed skins snagged in the scrub, then head down to the deep second cutting to hunt the third serpent that dropped on Bren's mule.
I step clear of the overhang's drop zone and turn to face the serpent behind me, casting Arcane Wave at it.

I head back to the weighing shed on the top terrace to report the third serpent killed to the quarry master, then return to the Guild hall in Alderwatch to turn in the Serpents on the Haul Road contract.
I ask the clerk what contracts are on the board suitable for a Novice mage.
I take the Clear the Old Crown Catacombs Level 1 slip from the board and ask the clerk to register it as my active contract.
I head to the temple close and find the Temple Wardens at the undercroft door, showing my Guild plate to get the key to the catacombs.
I unlock the undercroft door with the bright key and enter the catacombs, staff ready, keeping light and noise low.
I turn back to the Temple Warden and say, "The undercroft door is unlocked — I'm ready to go down into the catacombs now. Open the way for me."
I unlock the undercroft door with the bright key and step inside, heading down the stairs into the catacombs.
I enter the Old Crown Catacombs — I'm going in.
I cast Arcane Wave at the two skeletons in the chamber's far half, hitting both together.
I gather the bone and grave dust, then follow the corridor sloping down past the chamber's far side, watching for more movement.
